pred_reasoning_trace: An 82-year-old man presented with painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration without systemic symptoms. His history included glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty; medications were dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride. Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis with ipsilateral hydrocele. After 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate for presumed orchiepididymitis, swelling persisted. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology and revealed new bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement measuring 15×12 mm on the right and 27×18 mm on the left, with homogeneous attenuation; these nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier. An 18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake (SUVmax 25.5) in the right testis but no uptake in the adrenal glands. Laboratory evaluation revealed normal electrolytes, blood count, iron studies, protein electrophoresis, glucose, renal and liver function, thyroid profile, LDH, and β2-microglobulin. Serologies were negative for active HCV and EBV (positive for past EBV). Clinically, he had no asthenia, headaches, abdominal pain, striae, or “buffalo hump,” and his blood pressure was 130/80 mmHg without hypertensive peaks on 24-hour monitoring.
